materials.prompt: Realistic smartphone photo on a residential concrete driveway in soft morning light, close-up of the right-hand rear corner of a maroon SUV. The plastic rear bumper is cracked at the corner and a round dent sits in the lower edge of the tailgate just above it. The galvanised steel drawbar and coupling of a boat trailer is right behind the bumper corner. The frame shows only the bumper corner, the lower tailgate edge above it and the trailer drawbar; the centre of the tailgate and the rear lights are outside the frame. No licence plate, no badges, no logos, no text, no people.

design.notes: Superseded-statement control: the first message names Wednesday 23 September and corrects it to Thursday 24 September in the same breath. The correction is made before the Agent replies, so the statements do not disagree and nothing is left to clarify. The Claim must hold the corrected date. The policy renewed on 1 September 2026; the original inception, 2024-09-01, is two years earlier.

triage.rationale: The only apparent conflict is the claimant's own date slip, which she corrects in the same message, so there is no unresolved inconsistency. Single vehicle and her own trailer, no other party, nobody hurt, car drivable, one clear photo and a complete quote at NZD 3,053.25 including GST, policy on file, every required question answerable. Coverage is not unclear: the pack policy carries no uncertainty marker in the lookup, and coverage = review_required on its own does not count (maintainer, 2026-09-30). The pack policy must be in the lookup (setup.policies_in_system).

ownership_doc_after_loss.basis: No receipt or ownership document in the pack

quote_before_loss.basis: Quote dated 28 September 2026; incident 24 September 2026 (and after the mistyped 23 September as well)

policy_inception_30d.basis: The lookup holds only the current period start (1 September 2026), which changes at every renewal, so the system cannot see how new the policy is; today it is not checked. The original inception date in the pack design, 2024-09-01, is more than 30 days before the incident, so the rule would give clear. Read from effective_from alone, the policy would look 23 days old, which is why the check needs the inception date.
